why: ¶69 says 'our driver pulled up', and the landau was introduced in ¶51.
The villa 'stood by the road'. The party has come to see the scene, and Straker lived in a small villa near the stables, so this villa is plainly his.
¶69 mentions the paddock beside the villa. Calling it Straker's villa follows obviously from the context.

text: The long grey-tiled out-building across the paddock
why: This is a direct paraphrase of ¶69's 'long grey-tiled out-building' lying across the paddock.
¶69 mentions the steeples of Tavistock on the skyline.
The party gets out at the villa, which is clearly the trainer's house at the scene they came to see.

text: Thursday evening, the landau pulls up at a red-brick villa
why: It is Thursday (¶13), they reached Tavistock in the evening (¶47), and the carriage pulls up at the red-brick villa (¶69).
